投.meaning: At the village games, a shy <part>maiden</part> in a long skirt steps up to the line, curtseys, and swings a ship's <part>anchor</part> round her head. Off it sails, over the barn and the church spire. Nobody has ever seen anyone <kanji>throw</kanji> like that.
投.on: She spins round so fast before letting go that she stubs her <sound>toe</sound> on the line.
投.kun: Her prize is a hot <sound>na</sound>an, and she throws that too, straight over the crowd.

権.meaning: At the park pond, one <part>sparrow</part> stands at the end of a <part>diving board</part> nailed to an old <part>tree</part>, blowing a whistle. Ducks, swans and even the dog wait in line until it says jump. Tiny as it is, it holds all the <kanji>authority</kanji>.
権.on: When the whistle blows twice, even the guard dog slinks back into its <sound>ken</sound>nel.
権.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a <sound>mo</sound>le, as the sparrow drops a lead sinker off the board, plop, down to the <sound>ree</sound>f of stones at the bottom: a weight.

経.meaning: Across the desert rolls a <part>tumbleweed</part>, trailing a <part>thread</part> that unwinds a long scroll behind it. Every inch is covered in tiny holy verses, and a monk walking after it chants each line as it passes. The wind is reading him a <kanji>sutra</kanji>.
経.on: When the scroll runs out, the monk finds a little rice <sound>ca</sound>ke tied to the very end.
経.kun: A <sound>he</sound>n follows the monk for a thousand miles, pecking at each line as they pass through village after village.

古.meaning: On a tortoise's birthday cake the candles won't fit, so the baker writes a giant <part>ten</part> and adds zeros all the way round the edge. The tortoise opens its wrinkly <part>mouth</part>, puffs, and blows out one candle an hour. It's very, very <kanji>old</kanji>.
古.on: Its only friend at the party is a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala who is nearly as ancient.
古.kun: Afterwards they nap on one worn-out <sound>fu</sound>ton, and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> tucks them both in.

能.meaning: At the talent show, a stubby <part>teapot</part> waddles on stage with a <part>spoon</part> stuck on each side like arms. It pours itself a cup, stirs it, juggles three sugar lumps and catches them in its lid. The judges give it top marks for <kanji>ability</kanji>.
能.on: The runner-up is a garden <sound>gno</sound>me, whose only talent is standing very still.
能.kun: For its encore, it pours a perfect swirl of <sound>yo</sound>gurt into every judge's cup: done really well.

護.meaning: Every night, a <part>falconer</part> climbs the city wall and gives a short <part>speech</part> to her hawk: 'Watch the hen houses, the kittens and the baker's cat.' Then the hawk circles the town till dawn. Its job is to <kanji>safeguard</kanji> everyone asleep.
護.on: To see in the dark, the hawk wears a tiny pair of swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles.
護.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>! A <sound>mo</sound>le!' squeaks a kitten, and the hawk drops down to stand guard beside her.

看.meaning: A babysitter sneaks off to the kitchen, but leaves a glove propped on the cot: a <part>hand</part> with a big googly <part>eye</part> sewn on the palm. Whenever the baby sits up, the eye wobbles and the baby lies back down. Even from the kitchen she can <kanji>watch over</kanji> the baby.
看.on: She tucks a pink <sound>car</sound>nation into the glove so the baby has something sweet to smell.
看.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat stands on the cot rail as backup, keeping a look-out too.
